extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in commutative algebra (readers of Atiyah–MacDonald / Bourbaki style notes)
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions, and exercises about associated primes, primary submodules/decompositions, and results on integral extensions (Noether normalization, Zariski's lemma, Nullstellensatz), together with related exercises and corrigenda for Chapter 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for zero intersection via associated primes
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a noetherian ring, and (Ni)_{i∈I} is a family of submodules of an A-module M such that the intersection of the Ass(Ni) is empty, then the intersection of the Ni is the zero submodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Corollary 59 and Proposition 62; used to deduce uniqueness/vanishing statements from associated-prime data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes of a direct sum
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is the direct sum of a family (Mi)_{i∈I} of submodules, then Ass(M) is the union of the Ass(Mi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to finite index case and uses Proposition 62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes and submodules with zero intersection
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be an A-module and Q1,...,Qn submodules of M. If the intersection of the Qi is 0, then Ass(M) is contained in the union of the Ass(Qi), hence Ass(M) coincides with that union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use injectivity of canonical map M → ⨁(M/Qi) and apply Proposition 62 and Corollary 64.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of submodule cutting out prescribed associated primes (Prop. 66)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Ψ ⊂ Ass(M) there is a submodule N of M such that Ass(N) = Ass(M) \ Ψ and Ass(M/N) = Ψ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct N as a maximal submodule with Ass(N) ⊂ Ass(M) \ Ψ; use Lemma 56 and Propositions 57,62 in the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous realization of coverings of Ass(M) (Prop. 67)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is noetherian and (Ψi)_{i∈I} is a family of subsets of Ass(M) whose union is Ass(M), then there exist submodules (Ni)_{i∈I} of M with Ass(M/Ni)=Ψi for all i and with ⋂ Ni = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write M(Ψ) for the submodule constructed in Prop. 66 and apply the zero-intersection criterion (Lemma 63) to the family M(Ψi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: primary submodule (Def. 68)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a noetherian ring. A submodule N of an A-module M is primary if Ass(M/N) = {p} for some prime ideal p; then N is called p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Bourbaki's definition as stated; note later discussion about non-equivalence with other authors' definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning: Bourbaki vs Atiyah–MacDonald primary notion
rubrics_metrics.description: Bourbaki's definition of primary (Ass(M/N) = {p}) is not equivalent to Atiyah–MacDonald’s: example given where 0 is Bourbaki-primary but not an intersection of primary submodules in Atiyah–MacDonald’s sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses A = K[[x]], M = K[y] with a differential-type module structure; demonstrates anti-patterns in definition transfer between authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition existence (Theorem 69, Somaya Muiny)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a module over a noetherian ring A, then the intersection of its primary submodules is zero. More generally, any submodule N is the intersection of the primary submodules of M containing N; concretely N is the intersection of a family (M(p))_{p∈Ass(M/N)} with each M(p)/N p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to N=0 and applies Prop. 67 to singleton subsets ({p})_{p∈Ass(M)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite primary decomposition equivalent to finiteness of Ass(M) (Prop. 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A noetherian and M an A-module: the zero submodule is the intersection of a finite family (Q1,...,Qn) of primary submodules iff Ass(M) is finite; in that case Ass(M) is the disjoint union of the Ass(Qi). Similar statement holds for arbitrary submodules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Corollary 65 and Theorem 69.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction/extension behaviour under integral extensions (comment on Cor. 5.9 and Thm 5.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊂ B is integral and q ⊂ b are ideals of B with q prime and qc = bc = p (contractions), then q = b. Also ideals of A are maximal iff they are contractions of maximal ideals of B; dim A = dim B when B is integral over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are corrections/strengthenings and clarifications to Chapter 5 statements; proofs use localization and earlier propositions (e.g., Prop.3.11ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrally closed localization preserves integrally closed property
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is an integrally closed domain and S a multiplicative subset with 0 ∉ S, then S^{-1}A is integrally closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as a corollary to Proposition 5.12; short argument given in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for integral closure of ideal under extension (Lemma 5.14 consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A ⊂ D are domains and a an ideal of A, then D^* a = (D^* A) a (equation (42)); in particular D^* a is an ideal of D^* A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the proof of Prop.5.15 to control coefficients of minimal polynomials and deduce integrality of coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether's Normalization Theorem (Theorem 75)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A ⊂ B be inclusion of nonzero rings with B a finitely generated A-algebra. Then there exist s ∈ A nonzero, n ≥ 0, and elements x1,...,xn ∈ B_s algebraically independent over A_s such that B_s is a finitely generated module over A_s[x1,...,xn].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on number of generators; constructs suitable change of variables and a nonzero t to obtain integrality over a polynomial subring after localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zariski's Lemma (ZL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field and A a finitely generated k-algebra. For a maximal ideal m of A the field A/m is a finite algebraic extension of k. In particular, if k is algebraically closed then A/m ≅ k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Noether Normalization; used to deduce concrete geometric facts like identification of maximal ideals with k-points when k is algebraically closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete consequence of Zariski's Lemma (ZL2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = k[t1,...,tn] with k algebraically closed and m a maximal ideal, letting xi be the images of the ti in k via A→A/m≅k, then (a) π(f)=f(x) for all f∈A, (b) A = k[t1−x1, ..., tn−xn], (c) m = (t1−x1, ..., tn−xn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies maximal ideals with evaluation at k-points; used in Nullstellensatz proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullstellensatz (N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k algebraically closed, A = k[t1,...,tn], and a an ideal with associated affine variety X ⊂ k^n. Then I(X) = r(a) (the radical of a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to prime ideals and uses Zariski's Lemma and Noether Normalization; two proofs of an auxiliary claim are given to exhibit maximal ideals avoiding a given f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-up/closed mapping equivalence and consequences (Exercise 5.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: f: A→B has going-up (resp. going-down) if the corresponding theorem holds for B over f(A). For f_* : Spec(B)→Spec(A): (i) f_* closed ⇔ f has going-up ⇒ for any q∈Spec(B) with p=q∩A, the map Spec(B/q)→Spec(A/p) is surjective. Similarly for open mapping/going-down.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints relate openness/closedness of f_* to surjectivity after localization/quotient and to standard properties of spectra and direct limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat homomorphisms imply going-down (Exercise 5.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: A→B is flat, then f has the going-down property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent formulation: for all q∈Spec(B) the natural map Spec(B_q)→Spec(A_{q∩A}) is surjective; proof uses localization and properties of flat maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariants under finite group actions are integral (Exercise 5.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G is a finite group of automorphisms of A and A^G denotes invariants, then A is integral over A^G. Moreover, localization at multiplicative S stable under G yields (S^G)^{-1}A^G ≅ (S^{-1}A)^G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main point: an element x∈A is a root of ∏_{σ∈G} (t − σ(x)); hints give steps to express invariant fractions with invariant numerator/denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity of G-action on primes above a contracted prime (Exercise 5.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the setting of Exercise 5.12, for p a prime of A^G and P the set of primes of A contracting to p, G acts transitively on P; in particular P is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to showing for p1,p2∈P and x∈p1 there exists σ∈G with σ(x)∈p2, using invariance and contraction properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of Jacobson rings (Exercise 5.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A the following are equivalent: (i) every prime ideal is an intersection of maximal ideals; (ii) in every homomorphic image of A the nilradical equals the Jacobson radical; (iii) every non-maximal prime equals intersection of primes strictly larger. A ring with these is called Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use passing to quotients, localization, and maximality arguments; hints in text outline main nontrivial directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobson property preserved under integral / finitely generated extensions (Exercise 5.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Jacobson and B an A-algebra which is (i) integral over A or (ii) finitely generated as an A-algebra, then B is Jacobson. In particular finitely generated rings and finitely generated algebras over a field are Jacobson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (i) reduces to domain case and uses contraction properties; part (ii) follows from Exercise 5.22 about Jacobson radical behaviour under finite generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate Jacobson criterion using finitely generated algebra fields (Exercise 5.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalence: (i) A is Jacobson ⇔ (ii) every finitely generated A-algebra B which is a field is finite over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i)⇒(ii) reduces to embedding in algebraic closure of residue field and Exercise 21; (ii)⇒(i) uses criterion (iii) from Exercise 23 and considers localizations B_f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and equivalent conditions for locally closed and very dense (Exercise 5.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset is locally closed iff it's intersection of an open and a closed set, equivalently open in its closure. For X0⊂X, conditions equivalent to 'X0 is very dense' given; for Spec(A), A is Jacobson ⇔ maximal ideals very dense ⇔ every singleton locally closed point is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains detailed equivalences and proofs relating topological notions to algebraic conditions on prime spectra and Jacobson property.
